explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 9,113 to 6,110 characters (33.0%) and from 131 to 86 lines (34.4%). Six peripheral trees expand projection, checkpoint history, gesture settlement, renderer models, routing, and camera/UI interactions. [M] means modular structure, [C] call flow, [O] ownership, and [D] data dependency; these perspectives are mixed where useful. Connections attach to the corresponding concept lines, and positions leave gaps based on measured text dimensions.

Evidence is limited to the point definition, seed, and seven source texts embedded in context.json. MappingEditorRuntime.ts grounds history and settlement; shapeProjection.ts grounds shape eligibility and positioning; CanvasRuntimeContext.tsx and LocalAnchorStore.ts ground models, focus, and measurements; NativeRoutingStore.ts and connectionRouter.ts ground routing; MappingEditorCanvas.tsx grounds camera and UI handling.

Source-grounded qualifications correct overly broad readings of the seed: only the root container is locked, and parent lookup excludes the scene root; missing edges clear edge focus, while revision or selection-reference changes clear node focus. ConnectionRouter maintains mutable route and lane caches, so its boundary is described without implying statelessness. Routing disposal clears worker activity and results but does not clear owner measurements or router caches. Camera ticks call captureViewCamera; they are separate from semantic gesture commits, not free of controller calls.

Details absent from the seed include projection exclusions, exact clone rejection conditions, asymmetric source/target anchor resolution, retained model atoms, worker identity/job-ID guards, and input interception rules. Imported helper implementations, the worker body, controller internals, and application callback installation are not supplied; diagrams show their visible contracts and call sites without asserting their internal behavior.
